title: Short links
description: URL shortener for multi-tenant apps: create short links with random or custom codes, validated destinations, expiry, disable and click limits, an atomic click counter, a redirect route and a management API, with injected authorization and persistence.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build and Web Crypto (getRandomValues, randomUUID) plus the WHATWG URL and Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework-neutral core; mount the redirect handler on your short domain and the management handler under one API prefix.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlShortLinkStore with your query executor; on other databases implement ShortLinkStore with a unique code and a single conditional increment for recordClick.
Implement authorize(actor, 'create'|'manage'|'read', {tenantId}) from your own membership table.
Pass your own short domain (and app domain) in blockHosts so links cannot redirect to themselves.
Optionally pass isSafeDestination to call a safe-browsing service from the trusted server.
Mount createRedirectHandler on the short domain; mount createManagementHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins and your authenticate(request).
Optionally pass onClick to store click events (link id, time, referrer host, country) in your analytics table; never add raw IPs.
limitations: Codes are unique across all tenants because the redirect route resolves a code without a tenant; a slug held by any tenant returns slug-taken.
Destination checks are syntactic (scheme, credentials, blocked hosts); they do not resolve DNS, follow the destination's own redirects or detect phishing unless you supply isSafeDestination.
Click counts include bots and link-preview fetchers that issue GET; HEAD and other methods are refused and not counted.
onClick runs after the counter increments and its errors are swallowed, so click events are best-effort; the counter is authoritative.

The in-memory store is for tests and prototypes only; the SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, which is a single connection, not on every hosted Postgres or under multi-connection load.
No rate limiting; add request rate limits (see the rate-limit module) on create and redirect routes.
Production database correctness, session security, abuse handling and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: redirect GET {prefix}/{code} → 302 (not 301) with cache-control: private, max-age=0
unknown code → 404; disabled, expired or used-up → 410 unless reportGone: false
random codes 7 chars from a 57-char alphabet; slugs 3-64 chars, unique across tenants; taken → 409
only http/https destinations; credentials or blocked hosts → 400; client IP never recorded

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/short-links.test.mjs tests/short-links-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: destinations must parse as URLs with an allowed scheme; javascript:, data:, file: and vbscript: are refused
URLs with a username or password are refused
blocked hosts and their subdomains are refused, including case and trailing-dot variants of the own short domain
isSafeDestination can refuse a destination on create and update
generated codes use a 57-character alphabet without 0 O l 1 I and the configured length
rejection sampling discards bytes at or above 228, so each character maps from exactly 4 byte values
generated-code collisions retry and fail with exhausted after maxAttempts
custom slugs must be 3-64 of [A-Za-z0-9_-], are not reserved words (configurable) and are unique (slug-taken)
expired, disabled and used-up links resolve as 410 (or 404 with reportGone false); unknown codes as 404
click events carry only link id, time, referrer host and country; a failing onClick does not break the redirect
20 concurrent resolves with maxClicks 5 give exactly 5 redirects on the memory store and on PostgreSQL
other tenants and read-only members are refused create, manage and read as appropriate
list is newest first with keyset cursors and limit 1 to 100
redirect handler sends 302 with location, cache-control private max-age=0 and referrer-policy no-referrer-when-downgrade; only GET counts
management handler: create, list, get, stats, patch, delete, 401, origin check, no-store, 413 body limit and error mapping
schema.sql applies and the SQL store passes the core behaviors on PostgreSQL

changes: First release: core, in-memory store, PostgreSQL schema and SQL store, redirect and management Fetch adapters.
